description: Golden set for closed-set subtopic classification. Candidates are the real AQA GCSE subtopics for each topic; questions are written in the concrete style students actually see, so lexical overlap with the subtopic name is usually zero. Expected values are the candidate ids.

cases.topic: Bonding, structure and properties of matter

candidates.name: Ionic bonding (formation, structure, properties of ionic compounds)
Covalent bonding (formation, simple molecular structures, properties)
Giant covalent structures (diamond, graphite, silicon dioxide)
Metallic bonding (structure, properties of metals and alloys)
States of matter (solids, liquids, gases) and state changes
Limitations of simple particle model, nanoparticles

questions.text: Explain why sodium chloride has a high melting point.
Explain why graphite can conduct electricity but diamond cannot.
Describe how the delocalised electrons in copper allow it to be a good conductor.
Explain why an alloy is harder than the pure metal it is made from.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Describe what happens to the particles as it boils.
Explain why chlorine exists as Cl2 and describe the bond between the two atoms.
Suggest one reason why the simple particle model does not fully represent a real gas.
Magnesium oxide is formed when magnesium burns in oxygen. Describe the transfer of electrons that occurs.

candidates.name: Cell division and the cell cycle (mitosis)
Transport in cells (diffusion, osmosis, active transport)

questions.text: A sperm cell has many mitochondria. Explain how this helps it carry out its function.
An image of a cell is 50 mm wide. The real cell is 100 micrometres wide. Calculate the magnification.
Describe how water moves into a plant root hair cell from dilute soil water.
Bacteria do not have a nucleus. Describe where their genetic material is found.
Describe what happens to the chromosomes during mitosis.

candidates.name: The electromagnetic spectrum and its uses

questions.text: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 6 m. Calculate its speed.
Explain why light bends as it passes from air into glass.
Describe one use of microwaves and one danger of ultraviolet radiation.
In a slinky spring, the coils move backwards and forwards along the direction of travel. Name this type of wave.
